rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while ensuring strongly retained compounds elute. The moderate temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Only the first pair limits the score, so test a temperature change while keeping the gradient fixed to probe its selectivity. Higher temperature should also preserve the favorable last-peak time below 10 minutes.

Make the gradient slightly shallower at the favorable temperature to improve the first pair from R 1.41 toward full resolution. The last peak has ample margin below 10 minutes, so this may reach the maximum CRF without a time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already achieved; now seek a shorter fully resolved method. This gradient slope lies between injections 2 and 3, which bracket the first pair’s resolution threshold, and the endpoint remains above the observed elution window.

Trim the gradient endpoint while slightly increasing its slope relative to injection 4. This should shorten the method while retaining first-pair resolution near 1.55 and keeping the last peak inside the gradient.

Raise the gradient window by 0.05 while preserving injection 5’s slope to test whether a higher starting organic fraction shortens elution without sacrificing selectivity. The first peaks were well retained, leaving room to trim the weak-solvent portion.

Return to the lower starting fraction and test a slightly steeper, shorter gradient near the first pair’s resolution threshold. The last compound may elute during the final hold, so this run tests whether endpoint trimming actually reduces the last-peak time.

Make injection 6’s gradient shallower to recover the first pair’s resolution while retaining its earlier elution window. This tests whether the higher starting fraction can provide a faster fully resolved alternative to injection 7.

Reduce the slope to 0.07 organic fraction per minute, which should bring the first pair just above R 1.5 based on injections 6 and 8. This establishes whether the higher-starting-organic approach can achieve full resolution with a competitive last-peak time.

With maximum CRF already secured, test the unexplored low-temperature endpoint for an alternative selectivity regime. The unsigned first-pair resolutions at 40 and 60 C cannot establish whether an elution-order reversal occurred, so a colder run may reveal another useful separation.

Test whether 30 C separates the late cluster seen at 25 C while retaining the improved early-pair selectivity. A shorter gradient probes whether this colder selectivity regime can offer a competitive fully resolved run.

Test a higher starting organic fraction at an intermediate temperature to seek a faster alternative selectivity window. Warming from 30 C should spread the late cluster, while shifting the gradient window tests whether the early pair can remain resolved.

Lower the starting organic fraction and make the gradient shallower than injection 12 to improve the limiting early pair. The late cluster is already resolved at 35 C, so this tests a second temperature regime for full resolution below 10 minutes.

At 30 C, test a shallower gradient to spread the late cluster while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the longer elution time. This explores whether the favorable early-pair selectivity at lower temperature can support full resolution in a trimmed window.

Use a shallower gradient at 35 C to improve the early pair while maintaining separation of the late cluster. This tests a lower-temperature fully resolved alternative, with the last peak expected to remain below 10 minutes.

Return to 60 C and test a further upward shift of the starting fraction, paired with a shallower slope to protect the early pair. This probes whether window trimming can beat injection 7’s last-peak time while maintaining maximum CRF.

Test a slope of 0.085, just steeper than the fastest fully resolved method, with a high endpoint that avoids hold-phase elution. This closely probes the first pair’s resolution threshold and may slightly reduce the last-peak time.

Fine-tune the higher-starting-organic branch with a slope between injections 8 and 9, close to its full-resolution threshold. This should slightly shorten elution relative to injection 9 while testing whether the first pair retains R at least 1.5.

The fastest fully resolved branch is tightly bracketed, so now seek greater resolution margin without losing the maximum CRF. Extending injection 3’s gradient should improve the first pair while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes; monitor the narrowing third–fourth pair.

Use a slightly shallower slope than injection 19 to balance the first pair’s improving resolution against the third–fourth pair’s declining resolution. This should provide approximately R 2 for both critical pairs while preserving a last-peak time below 10 minutes and maximum CRF.

Shorten injection 20’s gradient and trim its endpoint to trade excess resolution margin for faster elution. The slope remains shallower than the successful injection 5, so full resolution and maximum CRF should be retained.

Increase injection 21’s endpoint one grid step to shorten elution while preserving more first-pair resolution margin than injection 5. This should retain maximum CRF and provide a compromise between speed and separation margin.

Preserve injection 22’s slope but end the gradient earlier to test a shorter programmed gradient with a final hold. Early-pair resolution should remain unchanged; the key check is whether the last peak still elutes within 10 minutes to retain maximum CRF.

Trim the endpoint and programmed duration of the fully resolved higher-starting-organic method from injection 9, with a slightly shallower slope to protect the critical pair. This should retain maximum CRF with all peaks inside the gradient and a last-peak time around 7.3 minutes.

Use the final injection for a conservative maximum-CRF candidate: this slope lies between fully resolved injections 21 and 22, with the endpoint safely above the elution window. Expect first-pair resolution around 1.77 and the last peak before 8 minutes; injection 7 remains the fastest demonstrated fully resolved method.
